one_liner: A brick-breaker game where the player uses drag a paddle to keep a ball in play, angling rebounds off the paddle and the side walls to break every brick on the board.
why_this_opportunity: Brick Breaker Worlds offers smashing through a wall of bricks with a well-placed shot and a screen full of multi-balls. Research (capability-screen): Brick Breaker Worlds: a shape in the capability catalog, screened against crazygames, gamedistribution, gamemonetize, gamevui, poki, y8, yandex at 0.73, with no observed market presence (estimates only). The opportunity rests on claim-bf0a6bc4fb and cites claim-0871e5f874, claim-45e8b8b427, claim-5d8a911ac6, claim-9b16b953de, claim-9c2fc37b75, claim-e619f4bcf5. Yandex Games is primary (audience regions by, kz, ru, tr; supports rewarded placements).

platform_set.rationale: Primary: chosen first by a person among yandex, crazygames, y8; the title is not shippable without it.
Secondary: CrazyGames is compatible from the same build; not required to ship.
Secondary: Y8 is compatible from the same build; not required to ship.

audience.player_description: A casual player on phone or desktop who wants to be playing within seconds, in sessions of about 5 minutes.

monetization.rationale: An extra ball after the last ball is lost is a natural rewarded moment; interstitials fit between levels.

mvp: Core loop: launch the ball, angle rebounds off the paddle and walls, break bricks and catch the power-ups they drop (multi-ball, a wide paddle on a timer, a laser that lets the paddle shoot), clear the board for stars, open locked levels and each world's star gates, replay for three stars; 32 hand-built levels in 4 worlds of 8, each world adding its own brick type or hazard (armored two-hit bricks, unbreakable steel bricks with sliding rows, a descending field, explosive bricks and falling embers) and ending in a boss level with a health bar
A single drag control: drag a paddle to keep a ball in play, angling rebounds off the paddle and the side walls to break every brick on the board
3 designed run-segments with authored difficulty on speed, density, variety, precision
Score and personal best, persisted through the platform's cloud save
A rewarded placement at a natural moment in the loop (continue or bonus), never forced
Interstitials between sessions only, never inside one
Yandex Games SDK: init, loading-progress, gameplay-start-stop, rewarded, interstitial, pause-audio-during-ads, cloud-save
out_of_scope: Multiplayer and any online play — networking multiplies the test surface and needs a server nobody has budgeted
Metagame layers: daily quests, battle pass, login rewards — retention systems are validated after the core loop is, not before
A cosmetics shop and paid customization; the unlocks the brief asks for are earned in play and stay in scope
Story, cutscenes and dialogue — text multiplies localization cost
A second mode; the release's content is the budget in concept.content_model.budget, and nothing beyond it
An IAP economy or premium currency
prototype_must_prove: A first-time player understands the drag control without instruction
The core loop produces an unforced desire to retry within one 300-second session
This risk is contained: Poki requires web exclusivity, so the candidate platforms cannot all be used for the same build; choosing is a strategy decision
The rewarded placement reads as a favour rather than an interruption
It holds 30 fps on a mid-range mobile browser inside a 100 MB bundle

success_criteria.label: D1 retention
success_criteria.rationale: Below this a short-session title without a metagame has no path to sustained portal traffic.

success_criteria.label: Median session near target
success_criteria.rationale: Shorter than this and the placements the monetization model counts on never get a chance to show.

kill_criteria.label: First-time players do not understand the control
kill_criteria.rationale: The title is scoped around one control scheme and no tutorial. If that scheme needs teaching, the scope assumption is wrong.

kill_criteria.label: Players do not retry unprompted
kill_criteria.rationale: Replay is the retention system here, in place of content. Without immediate retry there is neither retention nor an ad moment.

kill_criteria.label: The prototype consumed most of the timebox
kill_criteria.rationale: A prototype that needs more than 60% of the timebox is evidence the scope does not fit it, and production would overrun by more.

kill_criteria.label: Unplayable on mid-range mobile
kill_criteria.rationale: Most portal traffic for this audience is mobile; below 30 fps a reaction-driven loop reads as the game's fault, not the player's.

concept.core_loop: launch the ball, angle rebounds off the paddle and walls, break bricks and catch the power-ups they drop (multi-ball, a wide paddle on a timer, a laser that lets the paddle shoot), clear the board for stars, open locked levels and each world's star gates, replay for three stars; 32 hand-built levels in 4 worlds of 8, each world adding its own brick type or hazard (armored two-hit bricks, unbreakable steel bricks with sliding rows, a descending field, explosive bricks and falling embers) and ending in a boss level with a health bar
concept.gameplay_direction: Brick-breaker built on drag a paddle to keep a ball in play, angling rebounds off the paddle and the side walls to break every brick on the board. A session is a short run: launch the ball, angle rebounds off the paddle and walls, break bricks and catch the power-ups they drop (multi-ball, a wide paddle on a timer, a laser that lets the paddle shoot), clear the board for stars, open locked levels and each world's star gates, replay for three stars; 32 hand-built levels in 4 worlds of 8, each world adding its own brick type or hazard (armored two-hit bricks, unbreakable steel bricks with sliding rows, a descending field, explosive bricks and falling embers) and ending in a boss level with a health bar. Content: 3 specified run-segments in the prototype, 16 in the release, difficulty authored per unit on speed, density, variety, precision; progression skill-only; level-authored ramp.
concept.replayability: Mastery ramp: short levels on one difficulty curve, each with a best result to improve on

justification.session_length: 16 run-segments carry at least 300 s of designed play, 1 or more full 300-second sessions of new run-segments, the floor measured on releases a person judged shippable; at 3 sessions a day the replay system, not new run-segments, carries the days after.
justification.progression_structure: skill-only: 4 worlds of at least 4 run-segments each, each world gated behind the last, so there is always a next world in view and each one is a themed set rather than more of one list.
justification.mechanics: At least 8 distinct elements (obstacle kind, target kind, power-up) across the run-segments, introduced at 6 or more points, so later run-segments change what the player does, not only a number.
justification.replayability: Mastery ramp: short levels on one difficulty curve, each with a best result to improve on; each run-segment keeps its own best result to replay for.
justification.platform_expectations: Yandex Games, CrazyGames and Y8 list finished games beside this one: a release with 16 run-segments and new elements in later ones reads as a game, where the 3-run-segment prototype would read as a demo.

reusable_systems: Template boot flow: loading, menu, play, result
Template platform SDK adapter: one interface, one implementation per platform
Input handler for the drag scheme only
Content as data: every designed run-segment with its difficulty values
Ad-break service honouring the strictest interstitial interval, pausing audio and input
scope_decisions: One control scheme (drag); no alternative or desktop-specific input
Target session cut from 360s to 300s: short sessions keep content needs small and fit portal play patterns
Platforms chosen by a person, required first: yandex, crazygames, y8 (the opportunity proposed y8, crazygames, gamedistribution, yandex, poki)
Exclusion narrowed to the release budget (content): "A second mode; the release's content is the budget in concept.content_model.budget, and nothing beyond it"
Quality tier release: the content budget is 16 run-segments, 4 worlds, 8 distinct elements (concept.content_model.budget), the larger of the genre model's and the quality benchmark's bars
One required platform (yandex); every other platform is optional
Replay comes from a system (mastery ramp), not from more content
Asset budget capped at 30 unique assets (low asset complexity)
